claim: NullPropagatedOperands treats every SqlBinaryExpression as null-propagating and recurses into AndAlso/OrElse operands, which do not propagate NULL (NULL AND FALSE = FALSE, NULL OR TRUE = TRUE); so CASE WHEN x IS NOT NULL THEN (x AND y) ELSE NULL END has its guard dropped and yields FALSE where it yielded NULL, corrupting both projections and WHERE filtering. The existing ProcessNullNotNull at lines 2314-2321 already excludes AndAlso/OrElse; the new helper omits that guard (also reachable through the Not/Negate/Convert unary arm at 621). Executed against SQLite: 4 of 6 probes regress. None of the five new Is_not_null_optimizes_* tests uses a boolean-typed result.
raw: #1 🔴 Critical: `NullPropagatedOperands` descends through `AndAlso`/`OrElse`, which do not propagate NULL — dropping the guard turns NULL results into `false`

claim: Any boolean-typed clause.Result (e.g. a comparison like x > 2) is unsafe on SQL Server even after fixing the AndAlso/OrElse issue: SearchConditionConvertingExpressionVisitor runs after SqlNullabilityProcessor and lowers the condition to CASE WHEN <cond> THEN CAST(1 AS bit) ELSE CAST(0 AS bit) END, so UNKNOWN falls into ELSE and becomes 0 — the outer ELSE NULL guard that preserved NULL is gone. Provider-specific (SQLite emits the condition directly and is unaffected); traced via ToQueryString diff, not executed. Suggested fix: bail out when the result type is bool/bool?.
raw: #2 🔴 Critical: any boolean-typed `clause.Result` is unsafe on SQL Server, because search-condition conversion replaces the NULL branch with `CAST(0 AS bit)`

claim: The binary-operator null-propagation classification is hardcoded in the shared EFCore.Relational base with no provider seam (unlike SqlFunctionExpression's provider-supplied nullability metadata). String Add/concatenation is the risky entry: on dialects such as Oracle where 'abc' || NULL is not NULL, the new SELECT [A] + [B] shape returns the non-null operand where the old CASE ... ELSE NULL END returned NULL. Suggests an allow-list excluding string Add or a protected virtual PropagatesNullability(SqlBinaryExpression) seam. Anchor 50, read-only inference.
raw: #3 🟡 Medium: the null-propagation table is hardcoded in `EFCore.Relational` with no provider seam, but `+`/`||` concatenation is not NULL-strict in every SQL dialect

claim: IsNull(elseResult) is false when elseResult is C# null (a CASE WHEN t THEN r END with no ELSE), which is semantically identical to ELSE NULL and is treated as such by line 573 immediately above; the optimization is missed for that form. Missed optimization only, but the asymmetry with line 573 reads as accidental.

claim: In DropNotNullChecks, `return null; // true` overloads null to mean 'the test collapsed to TRUE'; the recursive `left is null ? right : right is null ? left : ...` chain at lines 607-609 silently depends on that convention. An explicit comment on the local function or a SqlExpression?-plus-bool return would make the invariant checkable.

claim: The new SELECT [A] + [B] concatenation shape depends on SQL Server's CONCAT_NULL_YIELDS_NULL being ON, whereas the old CASE ... ELSE NULL END did not; judged negligible exposure because Microsoft.Data.SqlClient sets it ON by default and OFF is deprecated (anchor 25). The reachable version of this concern is finding #3.

HashSet<SqlExpression> equality used for the null-propagated operand set: ColumnExpression.Equals compares Name, TableAlias, IsNullable, Type/TypeMapping and SqlBinaryExpression.Equals is fully structural including OperatorType; every constructible failure mode is a missed match (safe), no false-match path found (anchor 0).

Bitwise ExclusiveOr/And/Or in the binary arm are safe: T-SQL and SQLite bitwise operators are NULL-strict, and RelationalSqlTranslatingExpressionVisitor.cs:441-442 rewrites boolean And/Or to AndAlso/OrElse before this code sees them, so the only non-strict operators reaching line 626 are AndAlso/OrElse (anchor 0).

ExpressionType.Coalesce as a SqlBinaryExpression is permitted by SqlBinaryExpression.IsValidOperator but never constructed in the relational stack (RelationalSqlTranslatingExpressionVisitor.cs:449 routes Coalesce to the factory, which emits a SqlFunctionExpression tagged non-propagating), so the binary arm cannot wrongly descend into a COALESCE (anchor 0).

NullPropagatedOperands descends into SqlFunctionExpression arguments without distinguishing aggregates, so CASE WHEN [Key] IS NOT NULL THEN SUM([Key]) ELSE NULL END would collapse to SUM([Key]); judged equivalent in every constructible instance because any column legally referenceable in the test is a grouping key, constant within the group (anchor 25).

The nullable out-parameter on the early `return clause.Result` path: IsNull(elseResult) implies the ELSE arm was visited as nullable, so nullable is already true on that path; over-reporting nullability is the safe direction (anchor 0).

RestoreNullValueColumnsList(currentNonNullableColumnsCount) at line 539 passes the non-nullable columns counter to the null-value columns restore. Present at the base commit and untouched by this change — pre-existing, out of reach.
